ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2023-01-15
Provider: Dr. Carlos Mendez, MD
Department: Gastroenterology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Persistent jaundice and fatigue for the past two months that has not resolved as in previous episodes.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 20-year-old male with established hereditary spherocytosis, Wilson disease, and cystinuria who returns for evaluation of persistent jaundice. He has been seen previously in Hematology and the emergency department for similar presentations. He reports fatigue and a yellowish tinge to his skin and eyes for the past two months. His parents add that he has had several episodes of jaundice since infancy, usually following an illness, but the jaundice would resolve on its own. This time, however, it has persisted. He denies abdominal pain, but does report feeling full quickly after eating.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Hereditary spherocytosis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Wilson disease (diagnosed 2020-09-15)
- Cholelithiasis (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
- Cystinuria (diagnosed 2021-07-15)

His past medical history is significant for cholecystectomy at age 12 due to gallstones.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Cholecystectomy (age 12)
- Bilateral nephrostomy tube placement (age 14, for obstructing cystine stones)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Folic acid 1 mg daily
- Zinc acetate 50 mg three times daily
- Potassium citrate 10 mEq twice daily
- Pyridoxine (vitamin B6) 25 mg daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Hereditary spherocytosis, cholecystectomy
- Mother: Asymptomatic carrier for Wilson disease and cystinuria
- Younger sister: Hereditary spherocytosis
- Maternal uncle: Wilson disease (deceased from liver failure)

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: High school student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, he appears jaundiced with scleral icterus. Abdominal examination reveals splenomegaly without tenderness. No lymphadenopathy is noted.

LABORATORY DATA:
His complete blood count and reticulocyte count are as follows:

- Hemoglobin: 11.2 g/dL (Normal: 13.8-17.2 g/dL)
- Hematocrit: 33.6% (Normal: 40.7-50.3%)
- MCV: 82 fL (Normal: 80-96 fL)
- MCHC: 36 g/dL (Normal: 32-36 g/dL)
- Reticulocyte count: 6% (Normal: 0.5-1.5%)
- Total bilirubin: 3.2 mg/dL (Normal: 0.3-1.2 mg/dL), with indirect bilirubin being elevated
- LDH: Elevated
- Haptoglobin: Decreased

The peripheral blood smear shows numerous spherocytes with no evidence of parasites.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-05-15
Provider: Dr. James Wilson, MD
Department: Hematology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Chronic fatigue and intermittent jaundice, with recent scleral icterus following viral illness last year.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 17-year-old male with hereditary spherocytosis, Wilson disease, and cystinuria who returns for follow-up, last evaluated in January 2020. He has felt more tired than his peers since childhood and frequently requires breaks during sports. His parents report that he had mild scleral icterus during a viral illness last year, which resolved spontaneously. He denies bleeding, fever, weight loss, or recent medication use. He has never required a transfusion.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Hereditary spherocytosis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Wilson disease
- Cystinuria

Past labs from several years ago showed mild anemia, but no specific follow-up was done.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Cholecystectomy (age 12)
- Bilateral nephrostomy tube placement (age 14, for obstructing cystine stones)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Folic acid 1 mg daily
- Zinc acetate 50 mg three times daily
- Potassium citrate 10 mEq twice daily
- Pyridoxine (vitamin B6) 25 mg daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
Family history is notable for his father undergoing splenectomy and cholecystectomy in his twenties for similar symptoms. The father has had no symptoms since those surgeries.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: High school student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical examination today reveals mild scleral icterus, pale conjunctivae, and splenomegaly. There is no hepatomegaly, rash, or lymphadenopathy. Neurologic and cardiopulmonary exams are unremarkable.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory studies reveal normocytic anemia, elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), low haptoglobin, and indirect hyperbilirubinemia. Reticulocyte count is elevated. Direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test is negative. Peripheral blood smear demonstrates small, round red cells without central pallor. An osmotic fragility test is positive. Flow cytometry with eosin-5-maleimide binding shows decreased fluorescence intensity in the patient's erythrocytes compared to controls.
